 THIS MFA IS FILED UNDER SECTION 173(1) OF MV ACT AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED:19.01.2018 PASSED IN MVC NO.3302/2016 ON THE FILE OF THE 10TH ADDITIONAL JUDGE, COURT OF SMALL CAUSES, BENGALURU (SCCH-16), PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.
 THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT 1.

entities.text: MANAGER  IFFCO TOKIO GENERAL INSURANCE CO LTD
entities.label: PETITIONER

sentences.text: The claimant, being dis-satisfied with the compensation of Rs.2,44,600/- awarded by the Tribunal, is in appeal.
2. The fact that the accident occurred and the further fact that the offending vehicle was insured is not in dispute.

3. The Tribunal, on assessment of the evidence, has recorded a finding that the claimant has suffered the injuries to right hip and fracture of right acetabulum and has thereafter awarded Rs.2,44,600/- a compensation to the claimant.
4. The Tribunal, on an analysis of the medical evidence, has concluded that the claimant has suffered physical disability to the extent of 11.5% to the whole body.

It is the contention of the claimant that though the Tribunal did not dispute the fact that the claimant had suffered disability at 11.5% to the whole body, it has nevertheless refused to award any sum towards loss of future income on the ground that the claimant had not produced any document to show that he was not earning any salary.
5. The claimant, in support of his case, had examined Nanjappa, who was working as an Investigating Officer in Checkmate Service Private Limited, where the claimant had been employed.
The said witness has stated that prior to the accident the claimant was hale and healthy and was working as a Security Supervisor and was drawing a monthly salary of Rs.15,000/-.

In his examination-in-chief he has stated as follows - Sri. Saji Joseph vs Sri. Sunil Kumar on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39587915/
2 "4.

sentences.text: I further submit that, after the accident the petitioner was not in a position to move anywhere and he is taking further treatment as per the advise of the doctor and also he is taking bed rest and the petitioner is not in a position to do his work in our Company as a Security Supervisor."
6. Thus, the evidence of the Representative was to the effect that claimant was not in a position to do his work in his Company as a Security Supervisor due to the injuries suffered by him.

Though this witness was subjected to intense cross-examination by the insurer there is no suggestion put to this P.W.3 that the claimant was not in a position to work and that he was continuing in employment in the same position.
7. The claimant has produced Ex.P-23, which was to the effect that he was working as a Security Supervisor and during his working period he had met with an accident.
8. This evidence of P.W.3 coupled with Ex.P-23 leaves no manner of doubt that the claimant was not working after the accident.
The job of a Security Supervisor obviously would have a major component of physical mobility.

If the claimant had suffered 35% disability to the right lower limb,
it is obvious that his physical mobility would stand drastically reduced and the possibility of him continuing the said employment would be remote.

It is also to be noticed that even if he continue to work in the same employment, he would not be able to discharge his earlier duties and there would be a consequential reduction in the earning capacity.
9. It is noticed here that the claimant was not working in a Government establishment or in a public sector employment.

In this view of the matter, the observation of the Tribunal that the claimant had failed to prove that he had not continued in his employment or that he had become disabled to the extent of not continuing in his employment as before, cannot be expected.

As a consequence, it is to be held that the claimant had suffered disability at 11.5% as has been assessed by the Doctor, who had been examined.
10.
The Tribunal has taken the notional income at the rate of Rs.8,000/-.
The claimant did produce the pay slips which indicate that he was drawing a gross salary of Rs.14,240/-.
P.W.3, who has deposed on behalf of claimant also stated that he was earning a sum of Rs.15,000/- per month.
In the light of this, it would be appropriate to determine the monthly income at Rs.14,500/-.
11. Since the claimant had suffered the disability at 11.5% and having regard to the fact that claimant is aged about 50 years, a multiplier of '13' would have to be applied.
Consequently, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.2,60,130/- (Rs.14,500/- x 12 x '13' x 11.5%) towards 'loss of future income'.

12. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.40,000/- towards 'pain and sufferings' and Rs.30,000/-
towards 'loss of amenities'.
In my view, it would be appropriate to award Rs.50,000/- towards 'pain and sufferings' and Rs.50,000/- towards 'loss of amenities'.

sentences.text: The amount of Rs.45,000/- and Rs.40,574/- awarded under the heads 'attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance expenses' and 'medical expenses' is just and proper and is affirmed.
14. Having regard to the fact that the claimant was hospitalised for 46 days, it would be appropriate to take the laid-up period as three months.
As a consequence, the claimant is entitled for Rs.43,500/- (Rs.14,500/- x 3 months) towards 'loss of income during the laid-up period'.

15. Since the amount has been awarded towards 'loss of future income', the sum of Rs.60,000/-
awarded towards disablement is set aside.
16. The medical evidence on record indicates that claimant would require a further sum towards 'future medical expenses'.

In my view, it would be appropriate to enhance the 'future medical expenses' from Rs.15,000/- to Rs.30,000/-.
17.
Consequently, the award of the Tribunal is modified and the following sums are awarded as compensation :

sentences.text: Thus, the claimant is held entitled to the total compensation of Rs.5,19,204/- as against Rs.2,54,574/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.

19. The finding of the Tribunal regarding deduction of Rs.10,000/- from the total compensation amount on account of manipulation of documents and bills by the claimant is unjustified and is therefore set aside.
20.
The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded within two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
21. Out of the compensation amount, 50% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in the name of claimant in any Nationalised Bank for a period of five years.
The claimant can withdraw the interest accrued periodically.
The remaining 50% of the amount shall be released in favour of the claimant through Account payee cheque after proper identification and verification.
. The appeal is accordingly allowed in part.
